validation_summary.notes: Spec is structurally sound with correct dual-substrate architecture, comprehensive task coverage, and proper domain enforcement. Two blockers require resolution: (1) 11 task_classification mismatches between SOP and production, and (2) environmental condition modifiers in production contradict research RC-001 exclusion. 12 warnings for PS key inconsistencies, input name drift, material system ID mismatch, and task_summary count discrepancies.

cross_file_checks.details: All 36 task IDs in sop_modules.json have matching entries in production.json. Task sets are identical: TSK_PRFL_MOBILIZE through TSK_PRFL_CLEANUP. No orphaned or missing tasks in either direction.
Both files report 36 total tasks. SOP task_summary.total_tasks = 36. Production production_metadata.total_tasks = 36. Actual counted task IDs = 36 in each file.

11 tasks have mismatched task_classification between SOP and production. This is a blocker because the engine uses classification to determine task activation logic. Mismatches: (1) TSK_PRFL_MOISTURE_TEST: SOP=binary, production=substrate_conditional. (2) TSK_PRFL_CONCRETE_CRACK_FILL: SOP=binary, production=substrate_conditional. (3) TSK_PRFL_CONCRETE_CLEAN: SOP=binary, production=substrate_conditional. (4) TSK_PRFL_WOOD_MC_TEST: SOP=binary, production=substrate_conditional. (5) TSK_PRFL_WOOD_CLEAN: SOP=binary, production=substrate_conditional. (6) TSK_PRFL_PRIME_WOOD_ROLL: SOP=coating_conditional, production=substrate_conditional. (7) TSK_PRFL_PRIME_WOOD_BRUSH: SOP=coating_conditional, production=substrate_conditional. (8) TSK_PRFL_PRIME_MOISTURE_MITIGATING: SOP=coating_conditional, production=condition_conditional. (9) TSK_PRFL_STEP_DETAIL: SOP=coating_conditional, production=condition_conditional. (10) TSK_PRFL_ANTI_SLIP_BROADCAST_FIELD: SOP=always, production=binary. (11) TSK_PRFL_ANTI_SLIP_BROADCAST_STEPS: SOP=always, production=condition_conditional.
cross_file_checks.recommended_fix: Align classifications. Production values are generally more precise than SOP values. Recommended resolutions: (1-5) Concrete-only tasks should be substrate_conditional (production is correct). (6-7) Wood primer tasks are substrate+coating conditional — use substrate_conditional since substrate is the primary branch. (8) Moisture-mitigating primer is condition_conditional (production is correct). (9) Step detail is condition_conditional on has_steps (production is correct). (10) Anti-slip field broadcast is mandatory/always per KD-005 — SOP value 'always' is correct, production should change from 'binary' to 'always'. (11) Anti-slip steps is condition_conditional on has_steps — production is correct.

cross_file_checks.details: SOP task_summary breakdown (16 binary, 16 coating_conditional, 2 substrate_conditional, 2 always) does not match production metadata breakdown (12 binary, 12 coating_conditional, 9 substrate_conditional, 3 condition_conditional). Both sum to 36, but the per-classification counts reflect the classification mismatches in XF-003. After classification alignment, both summaries must be updated.

All 36 tasks have matching unit_of_measure between SOP and production. FIXED tasks match (MOBILIZE, AREA_PREP, REMOVE_PROTECTION, REPLACE_FURNITURE, FINAL_INSPECTION, CLEANUP). SF tasks match. LF tasks match. EA tasks match.

Resolution.json proposed_systems use short IDs (SYS_PRIMER_ALKALI_MASONRY, SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_EXT, SYS_FINISH_PORCH_ENAMEL, etc.) while materials.json uses fully qualified IDs with context prefix (SYS_EXT_PRFL_PRIMER_ALKALI_MASONRY, SYS_EXT_PRFL_PRIMER_WOOD_EXT, SYS_EXT_PRFL_FINISH_PORCH_ENAMEL, etc.). All 9 systems are present in both files and the mapping is 1:1, but the ID format diverges. Materials Manager correctly applied the SYS_EXT_PRFL_ prefix pattern per the material_system_prefix in resolution.
cross_file_checks.recommended_fix: Acceptable divergence — resolution provides suggested short IDs and materials.json applies the naming convention. No action required unless registry enforcement is strict on exact ID matching.

cross_file_checks.details: All 12 PS keys in resolution.json paintscope_keys array match the research.json required_paintscope_keys list. PS_EXT_SURFACE_SF.PORCH_FLOOR, PS_EXT_META.ENUM.SUBSTRATE_TYPE, PS_EXT_META.ENUM.COATING_SYSTEM_PORCH, PS_EXT_META.FLAG.NEW_CONSTRUCTION, PS_EXT_META.FLAG.HAS_STEPS, PS_EXT_META.EA.STEP_COUNT, PS_EXT_META.ENUM.EXPOSURE_TYPE, PS_EXT_PROTECT_LF.WALL_BASE_PERIMETER, PS_EXT_PROTECT_LF.RAILING_BASE, PS_EXT_PROTECT_EA.DOOR_THRESHOLD, PS_EXT_PROTECT_LF.LANDSCAPE_PERIMETER, PS_EXT_PROTECT_LF.HARDSCAPE_EDGE.

Three PS key / input name inconsistencies across SOP, production, and resolution: (1) Wall base PS key: SOP uses PS_EXT_PROTECT_LF.WALL_BASE, resolution and research use PS_EXT_PROTECT_LF.WALL_BASE_PERIMETER. Production uses PS_EXT_PROTECT_LF.WALL_BASE. Canonical per resolution = WALL_BASE_PERIMETER. (2) Landscape PS key: SOP uses PS_EXT_PROTECT_LF.LANDSCAPE_EDGE with input IN_LF_EXT_PROTECT_LANDSCAPE_EDGE, resolution uses PS_EXT_PROTECT_LF.LANDSCAPE_PERIMETER with input IN_LF_EXT_PROTECT_LANDSCAPE_PERIMETER. Production uses LANDSCAPE_PERIMETER. Canonical per resolution = LANDSCAPE_PERIMETER. (3) Hardscape PS key: production uses PS_EXT_PROTECT_LF.HARDSCAPE_WALK, resolution and research use PS_EXT_PROTECT_LF.HARDSCAPE_EDGE. Canonical per resolution = HARDSCAPE_EDGE.
cross_file_checks.recommended_fix: Align SOP and production PS keys to resolution canonical values: (1) Change SOP and production WALL_BASE to WALL_BASE_PERIMETER. (2) Change SOP LANDSCAPE_EDGE to LANDSCAPE_PERIMETER, update input name to IN_LF_EXT_PROTECT_LANDSCAPE_PERIMETER. (3) Change production HARDSCAPE_WALK to HARDSCAPE_EDGE, update input name to match.

cross_file_checks.details: Primary surface input name differs between SOP and production/resolution. SOP uses IN_SF_EXT_SURFACE_PORCH_FLOOR throughout all modules. Resolution and production use IN_SF_PORCH_FLOOR. Canonical per resolution = IN_SF_PORCH_FLOOR.
cross_file_checks.recommended_fix: Change all SOP references from IN_SF_EXT_SURFACE_PORCH_FLOOR to IN_SF_PORCH_FLOOR to match resolution canonical input name.

cross_file_checks.details: Step count input name: SOP uses IN_EA_EXT_STEP_COUNT with PS_EXT_DETAIL_EA.STEP_COUNT. Resolution uses IN_EA_STEP_COUNT with PS_EXT_META.EA.STEP_COUNT. Production uses IN_EA_PORCH_STEPS (a third variant). Three different input names for the same measurement.
cross_file_checks.recommended_fix: Align to resolution canonical: IN_EA_STEP_COUNT with PS_EXT_META.EA.STEP_COUNT.

cross_file_checks.details: Resolution proposes 5 round configurations (ROUND_PRFL_CONCRETE_PORCH_ENAMEL, ROUND_PRFL_WOOD_PORCH_ENAMEL, ROUND_PRFL_ACRYLIC_SEALER, ROUND_PRFL_CONCRETE_STAIN, ROUND_PRFL_POLYUREA). Materials.json coverage_profiles cover all 5 coating system paths with matching coat counts. Production quality_effects coat counts are consistent.

Production defines 4 factor_modifiers (FAC_PRFL_COATING_SYSTEM, FAC_PRFL_EXPOSURE_TYPE, FAC_EXT_SUN_EXPOSURE, FAC_EXT_SURFACE_TEMP). All use division formula (effective_rate = base_rate / modifier). Max combined modifier = 1.461x, well under 4.0x cap.

convention_checks.details: All task IDs use TSK_PRFL_ prefix. All module IDs use MOD_PRFL_ prefix. All consumable IDs use CON_ prefix (never CONS_). All factor IDs use FAC_ prefix. Context prefix PRFL is unique, no collision with existing prefixes.
All UOM values are uppercase: SF, LF, EA, FIXED, ROLL, SHEET, QT, GAL. No lowercase unit values found.
All module phase values are valid: setup, prep, prime, apply, cleanup. No prohibited values (protect, protection) found.
Research failure_modes use correct severity values: critical, major. No prohibited values (high, medium, low, WARN) found.
All consumable categories are valid: applicator, protection, prep, abrasive, fill_material, tool. No prohibited categories found.

Resolution.json applicable_enums.task_classification proposes values [binary, cs_conditional, cs_scaled] with cs_ prefix for coating-system-driven classification. However, SOP uses [binary, coating_conditional, substrate_conditional, always] and production uses [binary, coating_conditional, substrate_conditional, condition_conditional]. Neither downstream file adopted the cs_ prefix convention. The actual classification values used are more descriptive and should be formalized.
convention_checks.recommended_fix: Update resolution applicable_enums.task_classification to match actual downstream usage: [binary, coating_conditional, substrate_conditional, condition_conditional, always]. Or align downstream to use cs_ prefix consistently.

convention_checks.details: All sheen values in materials.json are single values: satin, semi-gloss, gloss, n/a. No compound sheens found.

domain_checks.details: TSK_PRFL_ANTI_SLIP_BROADCAST_FIELD exists in both SOP and production with empty applies_when (always active). TSK_PRFL_ANTI_SLIP_BROADCAST_STEPS exists with applies_when: has_steps=true. SOP classifies field broadcast as 'always' (correct per KD-005). Anti-slip aggregate is properly enforced as mandatory for all exterior floor coatings.

TSK_PRFL_MOISTURE_TEST exists with applies_when: substrate_type=concrete. Hard stop condition documented (MVER > 5 lbs OR RH > 85%). Contingency task TSK_PRFL_PRIME_MOISTURE_MITIGATING exists for failed moisture tests. MOD_PRFL_MOISTURE_TEST module is properly conditional on substrate_type=concrete.

TSK_PRFL_SEALER_TOPCOAT exists with applies_when: coating_system=concrete_stain. SOP correctly marks it as coating_conditional. Material system SYS_EXT_PRFL_FINISH_SEALER_TOPCOAT exists in materials.json. Research KD-009 documents this requirement. Sealer topcoat is properly enforced.

MOD_PRFL_PRIME applies_when is restricted to coating_system: [porch_enamel, polyurea]. Acrylic sealer and concrete stain are not listed, meaning they skip the prime module. SOP module description explicitly states self-priming systems skip this module. Research RF-012 and KD-004 document this correctly.

TSK_PRFL_PRIME_POLYUREA exists with applies_when: substrate_type=concrete, coating_system=polyurea. SOP description mandates manufacturer-specific basecoat. Material system SYS_EXT_PRFL_PRIMER_POLYUREA exists in materials.json with product_role=primer and notes about manufacturer pairing. Research documents polyurea system-specific primer requirement.

Epoxy is excluded from coating_system enum values in all files. Resolution applicable_enums.coating_system.prohibited = [epoxy]. No epoxy coating tasks, no epoxy material systems, no epoxy round configurations exist. The word 'epoxy' appears only in: (1) research exclusion documentation, (2) crack filler product descriptions (epoxy crack filler is a prep material, not a coating system), (3) moisture-mitigating primer description (epoxy-based primer is a contingency product, not an epoxy floor coating). All correct contextual usage.

No height modifier (FAC_EXT_ACCESS or similar) exists in production.json factor_modifiers. Research KD-007 explicitly states no height modifier — ground-level work. Production metadata confirms no_height_modifier context. Consistent across all files.

Coating system compatibility rules properly enforced: concrete_stain, acrylic_sealer, and polyurea are concrete-only (applies_when includes substrate_type=concrete). porch_enamel is available for both substrates. No wood substrate tasks reference concrete-only coating systems. Materials.json substrate_states correctly restrict concrete-only systems to SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY.

Research RC-001 explicitly EXCLUDES environmental conditions from estimation modifiers, stating they are 'site-level, unpredictable at bid time, and belong in SOP procedure notes only.' However, production.json includes two environmental modifiers: FAC_EXT_SUN_EXPOSURE (shade/partial_sun/full_sun) and FAC_EXT_SURFACE_TEMP (optimal/cold_surface/hot_surface). These directly contradict the research correction. FAC_PRFL_EXPOSURE_TYPE (covered_porch/open_patio) may also be considered environmental, though the research notes for estimation engineer mention it as a recommendation modifier only.
domain_checks.recommended_fix: Remove FAC_EXT_SUN_EXPOSURE and FAC_EXT_SURFACE_TEMP from production.json factor_modifiers per RC-001. If these are deliberately added by Estimation Engineer as an override of the research position, document the override rationale. FAC_PRFL_EXPOSURE_TYPE is a borderline case — it is a known property at bid time (covered vs open) unlike sun/temp which vary by day. Consider retaining FAC_PRFL_EXPOSURE_TYPE and FAC_PRFL_COATING_SYSTEM only.

domain_checks.details: Maximum combined modifier is 1.461x (concrete_stain 1.10 x open_patio 1.05 x full_sun 1.15 x cold_surface 1.10). Well under 4.0x stacking cap. All modifier stacking examples in production use correct multiplicative formula.

All 4 factor modifiers use correct division formula: effective_rate = base_rate / modifier. Verified in modifier definitions and stacking examples. Example: 200 SF/hr base / 1.1025 combined = 181 SF/hr effective (matches documented example).

TSK_PRFL_CONCRETE_ACID_ETCH applies_when differs between SOP and production. SOP: {substrate_type: concrete, coating_system: [concrete_stain, acrylic_sealer]}. Production: {substrate_type: concrete, concrete_prep_method: acid_etch}. The SOP ties acid etch to coating system, while production uses a separate concrete_prep_method dimension. Both are functionally equivalent but use different dimension names for the same routing decision.
domain_checks.recommended_fix: Align on one approach. The SOP approach (coating_system drives prep method selection) is cleaner and avoids introducing a new dimension. Alternatively, document concrete_prep_method as a derived dimension in resolution.

domain_checks.details: TSK_PRFL_PRIME_ALKALI_MASONRY_ROLL in production.json has applies_when: {substrate_type: concrete, coating_system: [porch_enamel, acrylic_sealer, concrete_stain]}. This means the primer task activates for acrylic_sealer and concrete_stain systems. However, research states: (1) acrylic_sealer is self-priming (RF-012, no primer needed), (2) concrete_stain is penetrating (RF-007/KD-009, no primer). SOP correctly limits this task to coating_system: porch_enamel. Production is incorrect.
domain_checks.recommended_fix: Change TSK_PRFL_PRIME_ALKALI_MASONRY_ROLL applies_when in production.json to {substrate_type: concrete, coating_system: porch_enamel} to match SOP and research findings. Same fix for TSK_PRFL_PRIME_ALKALI_MASONRY_SPRAY_BACKROLL.

blocker_list.title: 11 task_classification mismatches between SOP and production
blocker_list.description: task_classification drives engine task activation logic. When SOP says 'binary' but production says 'substrate_conditional', the engine may activate tasks incorrectly. 11 of 36 tasks (30%) have mismatched classifications. Must align before spec can be consumed by the estimation engine.
blocker_list.fix_required: Align all 36 task classifications between SOP and production. Production values are generally more precise — SOP should adopt production classifications for tasks 1-9 and 11. For task 10 (TSK_PRFL_ANTI_SLIP_BROADCAST_FIELD), SOP 'always' is correct per KD-005; production should change from 'binary' to 'always'.

blocker_list.title: Alkali masonry primer incorrectly activates for acrylic_sealer and concrete_stain in production
blocker_list.description: Production TSK_PRFL_PRIME_ALKALI_MASONRY_ROLL and TSK_PRFL_PRIME_ALKALI_MASONRY_SPRAY_BACKROLL have applies_when including coating_system: [porch_enamel, acrylic_sealer, concrete_stain]. Research explicitly states acrylic_sealer is self-priming and concrete_stain requires no primer. If deployed, the engine would incorrectly add primer tasks and material costs to self-priming and penetrating systems.
blocker_list.fix_required: Change applies_when for both TSK_PRFL_PRIME_ALKALI_MASONRY_ROLL and TSK_PRFL_PRIME_ALKALI_MASONRY_SPRAY_BACKROLL in production.json to {substrate_type: concrete, coating_system: porch_enamel} only.

warning_list.title: Three PS key inconsistencies across SOP and production vs resolution canonical values
warning_list.description: WALL_BASE vs WALL_BASE_PERIMETER, LANDSCAPE_EDGE vs LANDSCAPE_PERIMETER, HARDSCAPE_WALK vs HARDSCAPE_EDGE. Engine will fail to match inputs if PS keys are not consistent.
warning_list.fix_required: Align SOP and production PS keys to resolution canonical values.

warning_list.title: Primary input name drift: SOP uses IN_SF_EXT_SURFACE_PORCH_FLOOR, resolution/production use IN_SF_PORCH_FLOOR
warning_list.description: SOP references a different input name than resolution canonical. Engine input mapping will break if not aligned.
warning_list.fix_required: Change all SOP references to IN_SF_PORCH_FLOOR.

warning_list.title: Environmental modifiers in production contradict research RC-001 exclusion
warning_list.description: FAC_EXT_SUN_EXPOSURE and FAC_EXT_SURFACE_TEMP are environmental conditions explicitly excluded by research correction RC-001. If these are intentional overrides, they need documented justification. If unintentional, they should be removed.
warning_list.fix_required: Either remove FAC_EXT_SUN_EXPOSURE and FAC_EXT_SURFACE_TEMP from production, or document explicit override rationale with research team approval.

warning_list.title: Step count input has 3 different names across files
warning_list.description: SOP: IN_EA_EXT_STEP_COUNT / PS_EXT_DETAIL_EA.STEP_COUNT. Resolution: IN_EA_STEP_COUNT / PS_EXT_META.EA.STEP_COUNT. Production: IN_EA_PORCH_STEPS (no PS key documented). Three variants for one measurement.
warning_list.fix_required: Align to resolution canonical: IN_EA_STEP_COUNT with PS_EXT_META.EA.STEP_COUNT.

warning_list.title: Task classification breakdown counts differ between SOP summary and production metadata
warning_list.description: SOP: 16 binary / 16 coating_conditional / 2 substrate_conditional / 2 always. Production: 12 binary / 12 coating_conditional / 9 substrate_conditional / 3 condition_conditional. Will auto-resolve when BLK-001 classification alignment is completed.
warning_list.fix_required: Update both summaries after aligning task classifications.

warning_list.title: Resolution proposed cs_ classification prefix not adopted by downstream
warning_list.description: Resolution suggested cs_conditional and cs_scaled but SOP and production use coating_conditional, substrate_conditional, condition_conditional, always. The descriptive names are clearer.
warning_list.fix_required: Update resolution applicable_enums.task_classification to reflect actual usage.

warning_list.title: Acid etch task uses different dimension names in SOP vs production
warning_list.description: SOP routes acid etch via coating_system dimension. Production routes via concrete_prep_method dimension. Functionally equivalent but dimension name inconsistency could cause confusion.
warning_list.fix_required: Align on one routing approach. Prefer coating_system (SOP approach) to avoid introducing an undeclared dimension.

warning_list.title: Material system IDs in resolution use short form vs materials.json fully qualified form
warning_list.description: Resolution: SYS_PRIMER_ALKALI_MASONRY. Materials: SYS_EXT_PRFL_PRIMER_ALKALI_MASONRY. Pattern is consistent and intentional — materials.json applies the SYS_EXT_PRFL_ prefix convention.
warning_list.fix_required: No action required — this is expected behavior. Resolution provides suggested names; Materials Manager applies naming convention.

warning_list.title: SOP module MOD_PRFL_PROTECT phase is 'setup' — protection tasks have task_type 'protect'
warning_list.description: The protection module phase is correctly 'setup' (not 'protect'), and protection tasks use task_type 'protect'. This is consistent with pipeline conventions where protection deployment happens during setup phase. No issue, but noted for clarity.

warning_list.title: Resolution proposed MOD_PRFL_PREP_STEPS module not implemented in SOP
warning_list.description: Resolution expected_modules includes MOD_PRFL_PREP_STEPS (step prep conditional on has_steps=true). SOP does not have a separate step prep module — step work is handled within MOD_PRFL_APPLY via TSK_PRFL_STEP_DETAIL. This is a reasonable simplification but differs from resolution expectation.
warning_list.fix_required: Acceptable deviation. Step detail as a task within apply module is simpler than a separate prep module. Update resolution expected_modules to remove MOD_PRFL_PREP_STEPS or mark as 'merged into MOD_PRFL_APPLY'.

warning_list.title: Resolution proposed separate finish modules (FINISH_1, INTERSTAGE, FINISH_2, FINISH_SEALER) consolidated in SOP
warning_list.description: Resolution expected 4 finish-phase modules. SOP consolidated into MOD_PRFL_APPLY (single apply module with all coating tasks) + MOD_PRFL_ANTI_SLIP (aggregate broadcast). This is a valid simplification — coat sequencing is managed by the engine's round_configurations, not by separate SOP modules.
warning_list.fix_required: Acceptable deviation. Update resolution expected_modules to match actual SOP structure (9 modules, not 10+).

warning_list.title: Production acrylic_sealer quality_effects shows prime:1 but acrylic_sealer is self-priming
warning_list.description: Production quality_effects.acrylic_sealer.coat_count shows {prime: 1, sealer: 2}. However, acrylic_sealer is self-priming (no separate primer). The 'prime: 1' could be misinterpreted as requiring a separate primer coat. Should be {sealer: 2} only, or {prime: 0, sealer: 2} to be explicit.
warning_list.fix_required: Change acrylic_sealer coat_count to {prime: 0, sealer: 2} or remove prime key entirely.

recommendations.description: Fix BLK-001 and BLK-002 before proceeding to spec.json assembly. These are engine-breaking issues that will cause incorrect task activation and material estimation.
Resolve WRN-001, WRN-002, and WRN-004 (PS key and input name alignment) before engine integration. Input name mismatches will cause runtime failures in PaintScope-to-engine mapping.

Decide on WRN-003 (environmental modifiers). Either remove FAC_EXT_SUN_EXPOSURE and FAC_EXT_SURFACE_TEMP per research RC-001, or document an explicit override with rationale. This is a policy question that affects all future exterior specs.
After fixing blockers and major warnings, update both task_summary (SOP) and production_metadata (production) to reflect aligned classification counts.

Consider adding 'brush' as an explicit application_method for porch enamel (currently in SOP tasks TSK_PRFL_PORCH_ENAMEL_BRUSH and production TSK_PRFL_PORCH_ENAMEL_BRUSH, but resolution applicable_enums.application_method only lists [roll, brush_roll, spray_backroll]). Production has a brush-only task at 100 SF/hr.

Field-validate polyurea production rates (275 SF/hr) against actual residential project data. This coating system has the shortest pot life and highest complexity — rate may need adjustment after initial deployments.

Consider adding a note to production that TSK_PRFL_SEALER_TOPCOAT applies_when should also include acrylic_sealer if the sealer topcoat is intended as an optional second-system clear coat for sealers. Current production applies_when is [concrete_stain, acrylic_sealer] which may unintentionally add a sealer topcoat to acrylic_sealer projects.
